    15  /-!
    16  # Adjoint of operators on Hilbert spaces
    17  
    18  Given an operator `A : E →L[𝕜] F`, where `E` and `F` are Hilbert spaces, its adjoint
    19  `adjoint A : F →L[𝕜] E` is the unique operator such that `⟪x, A y⟫ = ⟪adjoint A x, y⟫` for all
    20  `x` and `y`.
    21  
    22  We then use this to put a C⋆-algebra structure on `E →L[𝕜] E` with the adjoint as the star
    23  operation.
    24  
    25  This construction is used to define an adjoint for linear maps (i.e. not continuous) between
    26  finite-dimensional spaces.
    27  
    28  ## Main definitions
    29  
    30  * `ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint : (E →L[𝕜] F) ≃ₗᵢ⋆[𝕜] (F →L[𝕜] E)`: the adjoint of a continuous
    31    linear map, bundled as a conjugate-linear isometric equivalence.
    32  * `LinearMap.adjoint : (E →ₗ[𝕜] F) ≃ₗ⋆[𝕜] (F →ₗ[𝕜] E)`: the adjoint of a linear map between
    33    finite-dimensional spaces, this time only as a conjugate-linear equivalence, since there is no
    34    norm defined on these maps.
    35  
    36  ## Implementation notes
    37  
    38  * The continuous conjugate-linear version `adjointAux` is only an intermediate
    39    definition and is not meant to be used outside this file.
    40  
    41  ## References
    42  
    43  * [Sheldon Axler, *Linear Algebra Done Right*][axler2024]
